title: Waving in the Autumn Breeze
description: Waving in the Autumn Breeze in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911), headed “Elevation of the Cross”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens (7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Wav-ing in the au-tumn breeze, Clap your hands, ye for-est trees, For the arms that now en-twine Nee-dy souls, were stretched on thine.

lines: Clap your hands, ye forest trees,
For the arms that now entwine
Needy souls, were stretched on thine.
And the cross that bore the weight
By the power that still remains,
Might, that wields the kingly sword;
Cross of Christ! we lift our eyes
For the arms that now entwine
Needy souls, were stretched on thine.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
